main.note: mainline extractors + verifier + native schema/verifier contracts

sarol.note: Sarol-variant adjudicator + the enum contract and rubric guidance it was split into (OQ8 resolved 2026-09-01)

combined_hash_recipe: sha256 over the concatenation, in ascending path order, of '<path>\0<sha256>\n' for every entry. Each entry sha256 is over the raw bytes of `git show <source_refs[entry.source].commit>:<entry.path>`.

output_vocabulary.contract: FIXED. The optimizer may edit every part of the rubric that makes it good -- boundaries, worked examples, tie-breaks, the worst-wins ordering -- but NOT the eight paper-verbatim class definitions (frozen in verdict_definitions_sarol.md and asserted verbatim in both judge-path files by check_paper_fidelity.py), and NOT the set of emittable labels, because the benchmark defines it and the scorer consumes it. The optimizer prompt must state this enum explicitly. A prediction outside it is an invalid output: scored as a miss and counted in error_class_counts, never a crash and never silently re-bucketed.
output_vocabulary.why_no_collapse_needed: This variant emits Sarol's gold vocabulary directly, so every gold label is reachable and 3-way macro-F1 is directly comparable to the published baselines. The mainline-plus-collapse alternative left 17 of IRRELEVANT's 34 instances structurally unreachable -- see the plan's Part A2.

runtime_pins.why: The extractor prompt loads the paperclip command reference at run time via `paperclip skill`; the in-repo SKILL.md is a 10-line stub. That reference is outside the frozen fileset, so without this pin two runs of one program version could diverge with no manifest diff.
runtime_pins.pin_history: 0.5.11 -> 0.7.48 on 2026-09-08 (Phil): gxl.ai serves only the latest wheel and 0.5.11 is no longer downloadable; the retrieval profile does not invoke the paperclip CLI at runtime (BM25 corpus, adjudicator-only), so the pin is bumped to the installed version rather than blocking. Load-bearing only for the paperclip/agentic profiles.

isolation_config.why: Setup pins (engine S2, adopted by PT-A 2026-10-01), one per sealed-session kind and platform: the fingerprint of what each session runs on (image digest and claimed version, identity rule, mounts by container path and role, profile and hosts, env names, posture, tools, model, option names, and for the optimizer its allowed-edit patterns). A session refuses to start unless its fingerprint equals this pin. Computed with `sarol_program.py --print-pins` under the retrieval profile. The linux-x86_64 pins (the VM) are owed: the image digest differs per platform.
